Tables that carry their context

Source: R/c4e_tbl.R
c4e_tbl.Rd

Functions of c4e return c4e_tbl objects: tibbles with one extra attribute, the metadata, recording the context of the data. The context includes the key column, the variable and its unit, the time step, the date range and the CRS. It also holds a registry describing every indicator column, such as its threshold, direction, percentile or spell length. Later steps of a pipeline read their defaults from it, so a value given once does not have to be typed again.

A c4e_tbl behaves like any tibble. Row and column verbs (mutate(), filter(), select(), rename(), joins, bind_rows(), [, grouped operations) keep the metadata. Dropping a column removes it from the registry, and renaming a column renames it in the registry. Verbs that change what the rows mean, such as summarise() and tidyr::pivot_longer(), return a plain tibble. The package functions that summarise rebuild the metadata themselves.

When stacking tables, dplyr::bind_rows() keeps the metadata of the first table only. vctrs::vec_rbind() merges the metadata of all of them. To join indicator tables side by side, use bind_indicators().

  • c4e_meta() returns the metadata, or one field of it.

  • is_c4e_tbl() tests for the class.

  • update_meta() sets or clears fields. On a plain data frame it creates a c4e_tbl.

  • tibble::as_tibble() removes the class and the metadata.

Usage

c4e_meta(x, field = NULL)

is_c4e_tbl(x)

update_meta(.x, ...)

Arguments

x

A data frame.

field

Optional name of one metadata field.

.x

A data frame or a c4e_tbl.

...

Named metadata fields to set. NULL clears a field.

Value

c4e_meta() returns a named list, one field, or NULL when x carries no metadata. is_c4e_tbl() returns TRUE or FALSE. update_meta() returns a c4e_tbl.

Metadata fields

  • key: name of the column identifying the units, e.g. ID.

  • unit_cols: further identifying columns, e.g. x_cell, y_cell.

  • variable, unit: the base series, e.g. "tmax" in "C".

  • time_step: one of "hour", "day", "month", "year".

  • shape: "wide" (one column per date), "long" (date, value), "lookup" (key by month) or "summary" (key, possibly by lag).

  • date_col, date_range: the date column and the period covered.

  • crs, source: coordinate reference system and data source.

  • indicators: one entry per indicator column, giving its kind ("flag", "excess", "spell", "pct", "std", "par" or "agg") and the parameters it was computed with.

  • transform, spatial_agg, window, survey, survey_cols, history, label, id_rule, preset: set by later steps of the pipeline.

Examples

x <- update_meta(
  tibble::tibble(ID = c("1", "2"), value = c(28, 33)),
  key = "ID", variable = "tmax", unit = "C", time_step = "day"
)
x
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#> # Context:  tmax [C], day; key ID
#>   ID    value
#>   <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 1        28
#> 2 2        33
c4e_meta(x, "unit")
#> [1] "C"

# the context survives ordinary dplyr steps
dplyr::filter(x, value > 30) |> c4e_meta("variable")
#> [1] "tmax"
